correctness.rationale: All hypotheses and area normalization are explicit. Translating and scaling makes D(δ)/sinδ precisely a moving-disk integral of the nonnegative triangle deficit. Boundedness near focal poles and \(O(|w|^{-3})\) decay give a global L¹ dominating function; indicator convergence yields the half-plane limit. At negative δ symmetry supplies the absolute-value form. Elliptic-coordinate focal distances/Jacobian and the two beta integrals give the exact coefficient and absolutely convergent positive central-binomial series. Executed standalone numerical checks are diagnostic only.

value.rationale: The canonical two-charge degeneration in Chui/Coulomb optimization changes analytic behavior at pole coalescence. The sharp positive weight-dependent first-order coefficient determines the true stability scale, distinguishes a cusp from a smooth quadratic loss, and provides an exact positive series in the symmetric reference case. These objects/coefficients are directly motivated by current weighted Coulomb theory; no arbitrary slice or unsupported downstream theorem is needed.
